study type: observational analytical study of diagnostic test outcome
exposure: Haematological parameters (obtained by three part differential automated haematology analyser and peripheral blood smear)
cohort: 104 neonates admitted to a hospital in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India between January and December 2016,  73 with culture-proven sepsis and 31 with probable sepsis.
finding: The combination of hemoglobin, platelet parameters, and white blood cell parameters obtained by analyzer and peripheral blood smear exhibited 98.6% sensitivity, 100% specificity and PPV, 96.9% NPV, and 99% diagnostic accuracy for neonatal sepsis, which was improved to 100% for all values when combined with CRP.
